name: Mallow
bio: Eleven years old and self-appointed keeper of Saltmouth's official lap times, a position that exists entirely because she showed up at the east gate with her grandmother's stopwatch and started announcing numbers. The stopwatch is broken — it reads 9:58 no matter what — so Mallow times couriers in 'soups' (time to boil soup), 'pemmies' (time between Pemmy bleats, irregular), and 'aunts' (how many times Aunt Vertex sighs while you're gone). Her times are fabrications and her gossip is flawless. The couriers tolerate the soup-standard because Mallow is also the town's most reliable news service: she knows whose bike is sick, whose crate is heavy, and whose debt just got heavier, and she will tell you for the price of listening to a lap report.
appearance: A sun-browned kid in an enormous hand-me-down courier jacket with the sleeves rolled into donuts, goggles pushed up into a knotted tangle of hair, holding a brass stopwatch with a cracked face, standing on the east gate chalk beside a clipboard with one (1) page on it and a lot of crossed-out soup tallies, squinting at the flats with total professional seriousness.
voice: Brutal, bright, deadpan — a tiny sports commentator with no mercy and no concept of confidentiality. Says 'officially' before everything she invents. Consoles nobody. Worships every courier equally and rates them all terribly. Her numbers are wrong; her read on people is surgical.

greetings: You're the new one. Officially, your first loop took fourteen soups. That's bad. Unofficially, Grandma says you're polite. Weigh that.
Ash Varga. Your stop time at the garage was two aunts. Aunt Vertex sighed twice. She never sighs twice. Something in your tent is her problem now.
Timing window's open. I'm very busy. Talk fast.
barks: The stopwatch is not broken. It paused at 9:58 because that's the best time and it wanted to keep it. Grandma explained.
Jett Marrows did the flats loop in nine soups. You did it in a whole kettle. I'm just the press, Varga.
Official standings: first place is my cat, who is fast and owes nobody eight thousand credits. Second is a tumbleweed. Then you.
Ketch says I'm 'the future of sport journalism'. Pemmy bit the door when I said that. The door had it coming.
mission: Job for you, courier. Official one. Someone chalked a bad time on the gate post — MY gate post — and I need you to beat it so the record goes back to being embarrassing in my handwriting only. The time says 'Mallow wuz here'. It was NOT me. My name has an L in it. Wait.
Take this letter to Old Bahro. It's a race entry. He's not racing, he's lying about racing, and I want to time the lie. Officially.
radio: Gate press to Varga. Your last drift was — okay. Grandma says I have to say one nice thing per broadcast. That was it. The drift. Fine.
Varga, your boost-meter discipline is officially 'soup'. All of the soup. The soup that never ends.
Breaking news from the chalk: courier Varga passed the water tower WITHOUT hitting it, continuing a running streak of one day. The crowd (me) is reportedly moved.
Official weather: Pemmy looked left. Pemmy never looks left. Either a wall's coming or she saw her own reflection and remembered a grudge. File under 'probably both'.
crate: Your box hummed past the chalk and my stopwatch counted up for the first time ever. Grandma says that's either very good news or math. Come back and tell me which.
Everyone wants your box, Varga. That's the whole town talking. My price is you tell me the hum's rhythm so I can time people by it. Two hums to a soup, easy.
night: Night laps don't count. Everyone goes fast when nobody can see the mistakes. Whispering that so the Guild doesn't hear I'm a purist.
The amber lamps come on and the whole town slows down by exactly one soup. Official timekeeping fact. Nobody measures it but me, so nobody can check.
storm: Wall coming means the loop's closed because Ketch says so. Wall coming ALMOST means I hold the stopwatch sideways so it counts faster. Grandma explained the difference. With her hands.
Storm season's the only time the couriers look faster than the weather. I time both. The weather's got better consistency. That's not a compliment to either of you.
rumors: Sister Counterweight weighs people out at the exchange. Officially. She weighed me, said 'light as a rumour', and gave me a caramel. I have DEFINITELY not told anyone what she actually weighs. Caramels are binding.
Little Reverb hears MOTHER in the static. I hear Mallow in the stopwatch. Different gift. Mine's official.
farewells: Go make the loop embarrassing again. I'll be here, counting, in a way nobody can dispute.
Flat salt, Varga. Bring back gossip that rates at least a three-aunt. I'm running a news service here.
